projects.name: Remote Museum Visiting Platform with Telepresence Robot
projects.description: This was a real-world collaborative project developed with the Australian Museum and the R&D department of Sage Labs, an internationally operating company specialising in social robotics. The project explored how a new telepresence robot could support remote museum visits, allowing users to navigate a physical exhibition space online while maintaining clarity, orientation, and a sense of intentional exploration.

details.challenge:
Project Context
Industry Context: Social robotics & telepresence technology
Institutional Context: Public museum environment
Company Context: R&D exploration for a new telepresence robot product
Use Scenario: Remote visitors exploring physical museum spaces online

Problem Statement
In collaboration with the Australian Museum and the R&D department of Sage Labs, this project addressed the challenge of making telepresence-based museum visits understandable and usable for remote users. While telepresence robots enable navigation through physical exhibition spaces, users often struggle with orientation, system feedback, and deciding how to explore meaningfully without physical presence.

Mission Statement
Design a human-centered remote interaction experience that enables meaningful presence, autonomy, and engagement in physical spaces from a distance.
details.approach:
Design Process
Understand: User Research/Competitive Analysis/User Interview
Define: User Personas/User Journey
Ideate: User Flow/IA
Design: Wireframe/Hi-Fi Designs/Prototype
Test: Feedbacks/Conclusion/Future Concept

Design Goal

Reduced Cognitive Load: Minimise mental effort by simplifying navigation, controls, and on-screen information.

Confident Remote Exploration: Enable remote users to confidently explore a physical museum space through intuitive telepresence robot controls.

Action and Progress Guidance: Help users clearly understand what they can do next and how to proceed throughout the visiting experience.

Spatial Orientation and Awareness: Support users’ understanding of their current location, direction, and progress within the physical space.
